title: Happens-before relationship — all rules, why threads read stale values without it
shortTitle: Happens-before relationship — all rules, why threads read stale values without it

s1_definition.profdef: The **happens-before** relationship is the JMM's guarantee of VISIBILITY: if action A happens-before action B, then everything A wrote is visible to B. Without happens-before, a thread can read STALE values forever — the JVM, CPU, and compiler are free to cache, reorder, and optimize without cross-thread visibility. **Rules**: (1) **Program order**: within one thread, each statement happens-before the next. (2) **Monitor lock**: `synchronized` unlock happens-before subsequent lock on the same monitor. (3) **Volatile**: write to volatile happens-before subsequent read of the same volatile. (4) **Thread.start()**: calling `t.start()` happens-before any action in thread t. (5) **Thread.join()**: all actions in thread t happen-before `t.join()` returns. (6) **Constructor**: end of constructor happens-before finalizer (and final field freeze). (7) **Transitivity**: if A happens-before B, and B happens-before C, then A happens-before C.
s1_definition.analogy: Without happens-before: Teller-1 writes "balance = Rs.50,000" in the ledger. Teller-2 reads the ledger but sees "Rs.100,000" (old value from their personal copy). The bank has NO RULE saying Teller-2 must see Teller-1's write. With happens-before (synchronized): Teller-1 writes and LOCKS the ledger. Teller-2 UNLOCKS the ledger → guaranteed to see Teller-1's write. The lock creates a happens-before edge: everything before unlock is visible after lock.
s1_definition.oneliner: Happens-before = visibility guarantee. Without it: stale reads forever. Rules: sync unlock→lock, volatile write→read, start()→thread body, thread body→join(), transitivity. No happens-before = no guarantee.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** The **happens-before** relationship is the JMM's guarantee of VISIBILITY: if action A happens-before action B, then everything A wrote is visible to B. Without happens-before, a thread can read STALE values forever — the JVM, CPU, and compiler are free to cache, reorder, and optimize without cross-thread visibility. **Rules**: (1) **Program order**: within one thread, each statement happens-before the next. (2) **Monitor lock**: `synchronized` unlock happens-before subsequent lock on the same monitor. (3) **Volatile**: write to volatile happens-before subsequent read of the same volatile. (4) **Thread.start()**: calling `t.start()` happens-before any action in thread t. (5) **Thread.join()**: all actions in thread t happen-before `t.join()` returns. (6) **Constructor**: end of constructor happens-before finalizer (and final field freeze). (7) **Transitivity**: if A happens-before B, and B happens-before C, then A happens-before C.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Without happens-before: Teller-1 writes "balance = Rs.50,000" in the ledger. Teller-2 reads the ledger but sees "Rs.100,000" (old value from their personal copy). The bank has NO RULE saying Teller-2 must see Teller-1's write. With happens-before (synchronized): Teller-1 writes and LOCKS the ledger. Teller-2 UNLOCKS the ledger → guaranteed to see Teller-1's write. The lock creates a happens-before edge: everything before unlock is visible after lock.

**One line to remember:** Happens-before = visibility guarantee. Without it: stale reads forever. Rules: sync unlock→lock, volatile write→read, start()→thread body, thread body→join(), transitivity. No happens-before = no guarantee.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The config reload service wrote `configLoaded = true` after loading.** Worker threads checked `if (configLoaded)` before processing. Without volatile: workers never saw `true` (JIT cached `false` in register) → processed with DEFAULT config → wrong interest rates applied to 10,000 accounts. Fix: `volatile boolean configLoaded` — volatile write creates happens-before → all workers see `true` AND the loaded config values (transitivity!).

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Thread-1: `data = 42` (non-volatile). `ready = true` (volatile WRITE). Volatile write creates happens-before edge.

**Step 2.** Thread-2: reads `ready` (volatile READ) → sees `true`. Happens-before: everything Thread-1 wrote BEFORE the volatile write is visible to Thread-2 AFTER the volatile read. `data` is visible as 42!

**Step 3.** Without volatile `ready`: Thread-2 may never see `data = 42`. JIT caches `ready = false` in register. No happens-before → no visibility guarantee → stale read FOREVER.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ HAPPENS-BEFORE RULES ═══

  1. Program order:    A ; B → A HB B (same thread)
  2. Monitor:          sync unlock HB next sync lock (same monitor)
  3. Volatile:         volatile write HB next volatile read (same var)
  4. Thread.start():   caller code HB thread body
  5. Thread.join():    thread body HB join() return
  6. Constructor:      constructor end HB finalizer / final field visible
  7. Transitivity:     A HB B, B HB C → A HB C

  ═══ VOLATILE + TRANSITIVITY ═══

  Thread-1: data=42 (A) → volatile ready=true (B)
  Thread-2: volatile ready read (C) → use data (D)
  A HB B (program order)
  B HB C (volatile rule)
  C HB D (program order)
  → A HB D (transitivity) → data=42 visible at D! ✅
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Visibility in Config Reload ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Banking Service                                   │
  │                                                    │
  │  Config Loader Thread:                            │
  │    loadConfig();                                   │
  │    volatile configLoaded = true;  ← HB edge!     │
  │                                                    │
  │  200 Worker Threads:                              │
  │    if (configLoaded) {            ← sees true     │
  │      useConfig();                 ← sees loaded!  │
  │    }                                               │
  │  Transitivity: loadConfig HB configLoaded write   │
  │    HB configLoaded read HB useConfig              │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — JMM Happens-Before ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Java Memory Model (JMM)                  │
  │                                            │
  │  WITHOUT happens-before:                  │
  │  CPU cache / register may hold stale value│
  │  JIT may reorder instructions             │
  │  Thread reads OLD value FOREVER           │
  │                                            │
  │  WITH happens-before:                     │
  │  Memory barrier: flush cache to memory    │
  │  Ordering barrier: no reorder across edge │
  │  Thread guaranteed to see latest value    │
  │                                            │
  │  Implementation:                          │
  │  volatile: MFENCE (x86) / DMB (ARM)      │
  │  synchronized: monitorenter/exit barriers │
  │  final: freeze at end of constructor      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The happens-before relationship is the JMM's visibility guarantee: if A happens-before B, everything A wrote is visible to B. Seven rules: program order (same thread), monitor unlock→lock (synchronized), volatile write→read, Thread.start()→body, body→Thread.join(), constructor→final fields, and transitivity. Without happens-before, a thread can read stale values FOREVER — the JIT may cache variables in CPU registers, never reading main memory again.

The most practical: volatile write creates a happens-before edge — and through TRANSITIVITY, all writes before the volatile write become visible to any thread that reads the volatile. This is how the "volatile flag" pattern works: `data = 42; volatile ready = true;` → reader sees `ready = true` → also sees `data = 42` (transitivity!). In banking: config reload flag without volatile → workers never saw loaded config → wrong interest rates. Volatile flag → instant visibility of all config values.
